ambiguities: Round-14 income: phase 5 runs after the last round, so passers draw 2 cards that count for Tiebreaker 1 (most cards in hand); rules do not say whether income happens in round 14 (assumed yes; effect tiny, ties 0.2%).

Open income relies on players remembering 5 rivals' shown cards: rules do not say whether shown income cards are kept in a public tableau or whether players may ask what a rival drew. Bots remember perfectly; humans cannot be assumed to.
Shown income cards that are later played, discarded and reshuffled back into the deck: rules do not say they stop being 'known' (assumed: knowledge only concerns cards still in a hand).

Income K rule: with an empty discard and a Bid deck under 2P cards the reshuffle is a no-op and K = deck/P rounded down (assumed; hit in 0.2 games per 6p game when all players are random, rare otherwise).
Rules 4.5 and 6.2 together do not say whether the crash tie-break counts bid values of cards in the Hype row only (assumed yes, as in the worked example); 3-way Hype ties occur in late rounds.
Section 7 (bot hints) gives a Hype projection of 'rounds left x 0.5': the rules give players no way to know the final crash, only a projection; not a rule, but the strategy depends on it.

problems.problem: Hype is still about 60% of all points (target 45-50, previous 55-64): the central twist swamps printed lot values, and the designer's own knob (lots 3-6) does not fix it.
problems.evidence: All-strategic tables: 56% (5p) / 64% (6p). E1 lots 3-6: 59%; E4 lots 4-7: 54% but forced passes rise to 7.1% and the lone-strategic gap falls to 18.0. E2 hand 5: 66%. Printed lot value 2 has the weakest link to winning (r 0.12) vs 0.33 for value 4.
problems.fix: Cap Hype per lot (for example at most +3), or count only the top 3 burned cards per category; or accept a Hype-led game and say so. Lot values alone (E1, E4) do not reach 50%.

problems.problem: Ablation tests: two of four rules fail the designer's 'lose by 5 points' test and two flip sign between 5 and 6 players.
problems.evidence: Full strategic minus ablated bot at the same table (5p / 6p, points): no-memory +2.7 / +2.3 (FAIL: open income adds about 2.5), ignore-hype -6.5 / +13.1 (inconsistent), ignore-crash +7.5 / +5.5 (pass), ignore-ties -7.0 / +2.6 (FAIL). Only the crash rule is confirmed at both counts.
problems.fix: Per the designer's rule, drop open income (or make it matter, for example reveal a whole hand every 4 rounds) and re-check ignore-ties and ignore-hype with a smarter full bot before claiming those twists matter. Untested: why the ablated bots win at 5p.

problems.problem: Skill gap is bot-dependent and mostly shown against random: at a 50/50 mixed table it is 11.8 points; a greedy bot gains only 12.3 alone.
problems.evidence: Lone bot vs 5 random (5p / 6p): strategic 30.0 / 20.6 (avg 25.3, target 20, previous 17.5), no-memory strategic 25.4 / 20.9, greedy 14.8 / 9.8. 3 strategic + 3 random: strategic minus random 13.2 (5p) / 10.4 (6p), avg 11.8 (target at mixed table at least 5, previous 0.8-2.3). Planner vs casual 23.4 vs 14.9 (5p), 19.7 vs 13.6 (6p): planner now beats casual. Planner vs strategic 21.5 vs 17.7 / 16.8 vs 16.6.
problems.fix: Improvement is real but the v1 and v2 bots are not the same bot (v2 samples rival hands), so part of the gain is the new bot. E5 (income 1) gives the same lone gap (21.3 at 6p), so the gain does not come from the 2-card income. The skill that exists is the odds estimate, not open income.

problems.problem: Last-round flips are still high at 6 players: the leader before round 14 loses in 27% of all-strategic games (designer target at most 20%).
problems.evidence: All-strategic 5p 20.0%, 6p 27.0% (mixed tables 16-18%). In the narrated game a 3-way 8-8-8 Hype tie was settled by the bid-value total.
problems.fix: Reveal the projected crash earlier, or freeze Hype before round 14.

problems.problem: Roughly a quarter to a third of bids cancel, so high cards feel like coin flips.
problems.evidence: Cancelled bids per game: 10.9 (5p) and 17.6 (6p) of about 55-65 bids placed, all-strategic.

problems.problem: Component count 82 cards (2 over target) and rules about 140 lines against a one-page promise.
problems.evidence: rules.md; E3 bids 1-11 (78 cards) keeps the lone gap 20.9 (6p) and seat gap 1.9, so the fallback costs nothing.
